clue.text: Daughter revered by Shiites, one cuddled by big mummy

indicators.note: something cuddled is held inside someone's arms, so the one goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: big means fat
ma is an informal word for mummy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter of a revered family is hugged by her large mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, is especially venerated in Shia Islam.

clue.text: American associated with Wells, artist getting in a mess

indicators.note: the artist getting in means going inside the other word

parts.note: William Fargo founded the American firm Wells Fargo with Henry Wells
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An American linked to Wells gets an artist into a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells suggests the writer H. G. Wells, but the partner is Wells Fargo, the American bank and stagecoach company.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble or hotchpotch is a mess.

clue.text: Call off time going up biblical mount

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means moving towards the top

parts.note: to abort is to call off

explanation.surface: A climb up a biblical mountain is cancelled because time is running short.
explanation.walkthrough: In ABORT the T 'going up' rises to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Tabor in Galilee is named in the Bible and traditionally the site of the Transfiguration.

clue.text: Displaced natives, aggressive people after next to no time

indicators.note: after places the aggressive people behind the brief moment

parts.note: a mo is a moment, next to no time
hawks are people favouring aggressive policies

explanation.surface: Native peoples are pushed out almost at once by warlike invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iroquois nation of that name was driven from its homeland in the Mohawk Valley.

clue.text: On returning, a husband, say, is caught entertaining woman

indicators.note: a group caught entertaining someone holds that guest inside it
returning means coming back, so these pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Back home, a husband is caught with another woman, a scandal in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman' is the definition, not part of what the husband is caught with: the reversed piece GEHA does the entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained as a hostess and entertainer, so the general word covers her.

clue.text: Place of darkness? You wait ages ____ turns up!

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the dark region through which the dead pass to Hades
fill the gap and the saying reads you wait ages before a bus turns up, with ere as poetic before

explanation.surface: A grumble about waiting endlessly for public transport, with a dark place thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in-the-blank: the gap takes two words, 'ere bus', which run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the primeval darkness between Earth and Hades bears this name.

clue.text: Having the means to exclude light, say, in hut

definitions.text: Having the means to exclude light

indicators.note: in places the spoken word inside the hut

parts.note: a shed is a hut
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Speaking from inside a hut whose windows are boarded against the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows fitted with shutters can be closed against daylight.

clue.text: As rude word, not entirely pleasant

parts.note: arse is a rude British word for the backside

indicators.note: not entirely means a word is incomplete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Calling a rude word not entirely pleasant is an understatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a mere linking word, but it is the chemical symbol, the definition. 'not entirely' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical element with symbol As is a notorious poison.

clue.text: Pretty environment for a namby-pamby set of paintings, maybe in four sections

indicators.note: an environment surrounds what lives in it, so the word for pretty goes round the rest

parts.note: pretty in the sense of fairly means quite
a drip is a feeble, namby-pamby person
art can be a collection of paintings, among other things

explanation.surface: A wimp gets a pretty setting for a series of pictures split into four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective meaning attractive, but it is the adverb, as in 'pretty good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided into or consisting of four parts, from Latin for four and parted.

clue.text: What it may be for a hungry bird?

definitions.text: What it may be for a hungry bird?

parts.words: What it may be for a hungry bird?
parts.note: for a bird, food is literally a larva dug from the soil, and the slang word for food happens to be that same word

explanation.surface: A wondering question about what a hungry bird might find to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works twice: slang for food in general, and literally the larva a bird pecks out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for food and also an insect larva, the very thing a hungry bird eats.

clue.text: Welcomer has installed superior musical device for visitor

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so the welcomer holds the other pieces

parts.note: a host welcomes guests
U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior
a segue is a smooth transition from one piece of music to the next

explanation.surface: A host has fitted a top-quality music system for someone coming to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying in a private home as a guest is a visitor.

clue.text: Northern town's boozer by a street of houses

parts.note: boozer is slang for a pub, which has a bar
a row is a line of houses forming a street

explanation.surface: The local pub in a northern town stands beside a terrace of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in northern England, usually just called by its short name.

clue.text: Acting, but troubled inside and lacking confidence

indicators.note: inside places the troubled letters within the word for acting

parts.note: doing means acting, taking action

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of but are stirred up

explanation.surface: An actor performs while inwardly troubled and short of self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' reads as the start of the description, but it supplies the outer word; 'troubled' scrambles the next word and 'inside' puts it within.
explanation.definitionFit: To be uncertain or sceptical is to lack confidence, as in a doubting Thomas.

clue.text: Lorna's piece of information to make a personal contribution

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so her possessive is her surname with 's
a bit is a small item of information, as in a bit of news

explanation.surface: Someone called Lorna offers her bit of knowledge to help out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of an English romantic novel set on Exmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to contribute one's own share of effort to a common cause.

clue.text: Plant lad yanked out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy pulls a plant out of the ground with a sharp tug.
explanation.definitionFit: A common name for the autumn crocus or belladonna lily, which flowers without leaves.

clue.text: Norse explorer doing nothing, funny fellow

parts.note: Eric the Red was the Norse explorer who settled Greenland
idle means doing nothing

explanation.surface: A Viking adventurer lazing about turns out to be a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Idle is one of the Monty Python comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian of the Monty Python team is a funny man by trade.

clue.text: Aussie to get hold of Yorkshireman?

indicators.note: an Australian accent pronounces the long a vowel more like the vowel in my, so this signals a spoken version

parts.note: to take something is to get hold of it

explanation.surface: An Australian is invited to grab hold of a man from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in an Australian accent, TAKE comes out close to TYKE. The question mark admits that the nickname is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is a nickname, sometimes affectionate, for a native of Yorkshire in England.

clue.text: Cars disturbing our rest

indicators.note: disturbing means throwing into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Passing traffic keeps waking us up.
explanation.definitionFit: Open touring cars are a type of motor car built for long journeys.

clue.text: Elephant maybe taking short step before my herd goes berserk

indicators.note: before places the shortened step ahead of the rearranged letters
short means cut short, so the step loses its final letter

parts.note: a pace is a step

indicators.note: something that goes berserk runs wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An elephant takes a small step forward before the rest of the herd stampedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims PACE to PAC, and 'goes berserk' turns MY HERD into HYDERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are the classic thick-skinned beasts, and that group name covers them; 'maybe' marks an example.

clue.text: Advice from Clarke-supporting Remainers? Listen!

parts.note: the advice of supporters urging others to pay attention is hear
Ken Clarke was a pro-European Conservative minister

explanation.surface: Pro-EU campaigners backing Clarke urge everyone to pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Clarke was a veteran British Conservative who backed staying in the EU, so Remainers supporting him would say 'Hear, Ken!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned imperative telling someone to pay attention.

clue.text: Good person coming in took control and made a bit of a noise

definitions.text: made a bit of a noise

indicators.note: the good person coming in enters the other word

parts.note: ruled means took control
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A worthy newcomer took charge and caused a minor stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves or paper that rustled gave a soft crackling sound.

clue.text: Trial being heard — man presiding at it?

indicators.note: being heard means spoken aloud, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: a pilot is a trial run, as in a pilot scheme

explanation.surface: A court hearing is under way and someone asks who is the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the trial: Pontius Pilate presided at the trial of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman governor presided over the trial of Jesus in the Gospels.

clue.text: Believer gives Zola greeting on street

parts.note: Zola Budd was a South African-born runner who raced for Britain
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A believer offers a hello to someone named Zola out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola looks like the French novelist Emile, but here it is the athlete Zola Budd, famous from the 1984 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the teachings of the Buddha is a religious believer.

clue.text: Foremost of pupils in an exam must be this?

definitions.text: Foremost of pupils in an exam must be this?

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the phrase for an exam

parts.note: an exam is a test, giving A TEST

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The top pupils in an exam surely have to be the cleverest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: P goes into A TEST, and the student who comes top must be the most able.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of apt, meaning most able or quickest to learn, describes a top pupil.

clue.text: Top lady abandoning dog in German city

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a terrier is a dog
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the top lady

explanation.surface: A grand woman leaves her dog behind in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany.

clue.text: One composer surprisingly able, another satisfactory

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something unexpected, so the letters of able come out in a new order

parts.note: another composer: Lionel Bart wrote the musical Oliver!
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: One composer turns out surprisingly capable, and a second one is decent enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns ABLE into BELA. 'another' stands for a second composer, Lionel Bart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian Bela Bartok was a leading twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: See 15
Probe filthy place occupied by tenant?

parts.note: a sty, where pigs live, is a byword for a filthy place
a property that is let is rented out to a tenant

explanation.surface: An investigation into a squalid home rented out to a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender surgical instrument used for probing wounds goes by this name.

clue.text: Made tough resolution to cross river

indicators.note: to cross something here means to straddle it, so the resolution goes round the river

parts.note: an end is a resolution or conclusion
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: It took toughness and determination to get across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of inured, meaning hardened or accustomed to hardship.
